item.title: An auditable multi-agent forum for scientific workflows with a computational MOF case study
item.description: Scientific research increasingly combines large language models, computational tools and automated laboratories, creating a need to link hypotheses, assumptions, artifacts and revisions. We present Core-Forum, a persistent multi-agent forum architecture designed to organize these records in a common research thread. item.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
item.description: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. item.title: The Inverse-Wisdom Law: Architectural Tribalism and the Consensus Paradox in Agentic Swarms
item.description: Abstract As AI transitions toward multi-agent systems (MAS), research paradigms operate on the assumption that agent collaboration mirrors the ''Wisdom of the Crowd.'' We challenge this assumption by formalizing the \textit{Consensus Paradox}, a phenomenon in which agentic swarms prioritize internal agreement over logical truth. item.title: Safe Recovery of AI Agents in Enterprise Systems: Preventing Duplicate Actions and Preserving Human Corrections
item.description: Reliable use of AI agents in enterprise systems depends on what happens after an action fails or its outcome becomes uncertain. Retrying can duplicate an order, while reversing a workflow can invalidate a person’s subsequent correction. The central challenge is deciding whether recovery is justified by the available evidence and still satisfies the business request. item.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
item.description: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). item.description: Despite the success of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), misleading charts remain a significant challenge due to their deceptive visual structures and distorted data representations. item.title: MetaNav: Metacognitive Vision-Language Navigation via Reflective Exploration
item.description: Training-free Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents powered by foundation models can follow instructions and explore 3D environments. item.description: Menstrual-cycle-related conditions and, later, menopausal symptoms are highly prevalent across the female life course and impose a large, under-recognized burden on quality of life and work, yet digital tools to support self-management are fragmented, hard to sustain, and unevenly reached. item.description: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. item.title: The impact of temporal resampling on the safety of clinical reinforcement learning: A simulated trial
item.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a type of artificial intelligence for making optimal choices. In healthcare, researchers generally use offline RL (ORL), where models are trained and evaluated from retrospective observational data. To accommodate naturally irregular clinical records, researchers often resample the data into uniform time intervals before training (known as binning). item.title: Opioid overdose deaths are declining in Chicago, but not every neighborhood is seeing the same progress: JSAD research
item.description: This report focuses on opioid overdose deaths in the Black Chicago community -a vital factor in the fight for Black prosperity and equity.

item.description: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University.
